title: PerformanceEvidenceValidator
responsibility: Requires matching current latency and memory observations for each executable unit, callable and runtime target without granting budget approval.

inputs.name: PerformanceEvidenceValidator.required.units
inputs.description: The array contains component manifests considered by required or validate. Only active manifests are retained; non-module runtimes are always executable, while a module runtime is executable if any owned file is unread or missing, no owned paths are listed, or a readable non-CSS owned file is not declarative.

inputs.name: PerformanceEvidenceValidator.required.files
inputs.description: The map associates repository paths with source-file records used to classify module manifests. Missing or unread owned records and empty owned-path lists keep a module executable; otherwise readable CSS-only or declarative code is exempt.

inputs.name: PerformanceEvidenceValidator.validate.input
inputs.description: Provides the manifests, path-to-source-file map, measurements, commit, and profile used by validate. A measurement can satisfy a requirement only when its unit, callable, target, tested revision, profile, and observed-value checks match the corresponding filters.

outputs.name: PerformanceEvidenceValidator.required
outputs.description: Returns the active manifests that need profiling according to their runtime and inspected owned files. Non-module runtimes always qualify; module runtimes qualify when an owned file is unread or missing, no owned paths are listed, or any readable non-CSS owned file is not declarative.

outputs.name: PerformanceEvidenceValidator.validate
outputs.description: Returns diagnostic strings for required unit/callable/target combinations that lack paired observations, or an empty array when every such combination is covered. Coverage needs observed latency (latency-* or browser-navigation-ms) in ms and a positive byte metric (memory-bytes, process-peak-rss-bytes, or browser-js-heap-bytes) for the same nonblank workload, with exact current commit and profile matches; observed values must be finite and nonnegative, methods nonblank, comparison boundaries non-fixture, and sample counts positive.
examples: reports.component.evidence-grid (module): profiling requires current latency and memory observations for the same representative workload; run its Harness profile check.
